Subject: Regional model-fit sprint proposal + identified quality gaps (EU & APAC)

Hi Eva / George —

Thanks again for the call earlier — this thread pulls together a lightweight proposal and surface-level findings from our quick post-call review so we can lock a pilot scope. High level: you shared examples for EU transaction descriptions (EN, NL, PL) and some APAC flows (TH, VN). Our initial validation shows good overall intent detection on the smaller instruct models, but two recurring issues popped up that would materially affect UX: morphological agreement errors in Dutch/Polish and tokenization-induced hallucinations in Thai/Vietnamese long-form fields.

Recommended starter model matrix (for the pilot):
- baseline: rlm-3b-quant (fast, cost-efficient) — use for short-form customer-visible responses and embeddings
- regional heavy: rlm-13b-sft (better morphology & context retention) — use for NL/PL/TH/VN candidate routes
- fallback: rlm-70b-dyn (higher-capacity; only for long-tail or fallback when hallucination risk is high)

Proposed evaluation metrics for the 2-week sprint:
- Exact intent match (binary)
- Localized acceptability (1–5 human rating; n=100 per locale)
- Hallucination rate (model asserts unverifiable merchant data)
- Latency P95 and cost-per-1000 tokens

Attachments: prompt sets and initial benchmark digest (attached). Also shared a Drive folder with the raw sample set and our preliminary model runs: https://drive.redwood.example/drive/folders/nbp-eval-2027

Next steps (suggested):
1) Sign off on pilot scope (this thread) — I’ve attached a short MoA with objectives and success criteria.
2) Share a sanitized sample of 500 locale-specific utterances (we have guidance in the prompt_sets zip) — NorthBank to provide by EOD Wednesday PT.
3) Kickoff call to lock telemetry and eval rubric — propose Tue Jun 1 10:00 PT / 19:00 CET (30 min). Marcus will join for rollout constraints.

Risks & notes:
- Data residency: if samples contain PII we’ll run in your VPC/private deployment; otherwise hosted runs on dedicated pools are fine.
- Regression concern: when we quantize smaller models aggressively some morphology errors become more frequent — this is specifically visible in Polish inflection chains.

I’ll wait for your confirmation on scope and the sample delivery timeline.

Best,
Ben

Hi all — quick technical addendum from the eval team based on the sample runs we ran this morning.

1) Dutch / Polish morphology: the smaller quant models (rlm-3b-quant) produce correct stems but drop or misapply inflection on multi-token entity mentions (e.g., transaction descriptions with merchant + location). That shows up as awkward grammar and occasionally changes meaning for compliance copy. We observed a 12–15% reduction in localized acceptability vs. control on a 200-sample probe set.

2) Thai / Vietnamese tokenization: long-form user-provided fields (notes > 40 tokens) sometimes elide or split compounds in ways that trigger hallucination when the model tries to expand abbreviations. Using a higher-capacity model with subword-aware tokenization reduced hallucination occurrences by ~40% in the small probe.

3) Prompt engineering: we recommend per-locale templates in the pilot (included in nbp_prompt_sets_v1.zip). Key patterns: explicit normalization step, local example pairs, and a short system message instructing the model to "prefer concision and avoid inventing merchant details."

4) Eval plan tweaks: add a 0–1 hallucination flag that raters can flip; collect token-level alignment for a sample of 50 cases to spot quantization-induced token mistakes.

Actionable ask to NorthBank: can you surface a small set of 10 "hard negative" examples for each NL/PL/TH/VN so we can prioritize model retuning? If you can deliver those with the sanitized set that will speed iteration.

Thanks — Neha
